_meta.purpose: Local, uncommitted permission allowlist for the two Suvarna execution sessions run unattended in /Users/Dev/suvarna/hq (Claude Code v2.1.239, --permission-mode dontAsk). Never committed: this file is .claude/settings.local.json, not .claude/settings.json.
findings_v2_1_239: permissions.allow/deny path rules for file tools only match on the canonical form Read(<glob>) or Edit(<glob>); Read(<glob>) governs Read/Glob/Grep/NotebookRead together, and Edit(<glob>) governs Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit together (confirmed via `claude --debug`: Write(<glob>), Glob(<glob>), MultiEdit(<glob>) and NotebookEdit(<glob>) are all logged as dead rules, 'not matched by file permission checks'). This template therefore never writes a Write(...) or Glob(...) path rule -- it would silently grant nothing.

Bash(<prefix> *) matches a Bash command by prefix, with the space before '*' significant (Bash(git status*) is a different, looser match than Bash(git status *)); a chained command (a && b) appears to require each segment to independently match an allow rule.

permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode is included per the L.15 brief but its effect could NOT be confirmed in this install: no lint/validation message appeared for it, but the settings loader also does not warn on entirely invented keys (checked with a nonsense key), so absence of a warning is not confirmation. The real enforcement in this template is structural: defaultMode is 'dontAsk' (never 'bypassPermissions'), and the deny list separately refuses any Bash invocation that itself tries to pass --dangerously-skip-permissions or a bypassPermissions mode. See INTERIM_RUNTIME_v1_0.md for the full account.

CODE-21 (review pass 2, arch §2.4): this template also backs $SUVARNA_HOME/config/claude-settings.json (the N-25 settings file, runtime_settings.claude_settings_target_path) -- the deny rules below cover both targets. The psql allow rule is narrowed to the exact reader-credential invocation form (bash -c "source ~/.config/suvarna/pgenv.sh && psql ...", the shape detectors._psql and monitor._default_credential_query_fn both use) rather than a bare Bash(psql *), which would also allow psql against any other connection string. Only Read(<glob>)/Edit(<glob>) file-rule forms are ever used, per the v2.1.239 finding above; mcp__<server>__<tool> deny entries are tool-name rules, not file-glob rules, so that finding does not apply to them.

Review pass 3 (B1/B2/B5/B6/B7/B10/S14, CODE-22/23/25/26/27/28): the psql allow rule switches from double to single quotes to match every role document (ROLE_COMMON:85, ROLE_ANALYST:50, ROLE_BUILD_OPERATOR:95) -- the two forms are different Bash rules under v2.1.239's prefix-match semantics, so the double-quoted form the swarm actually runs under never matched the documents' single-quoted form. The broad Bash(git push *) allow is dropped for two exact lane-push forms; Bash(python3 -m suvarna_tracker.* *) is dropped for five named safe modules (emit, monitor, hq_commit, lane_launch, events) plus census_run -- decide/decisions/runtime_settings are explicitly denied instead of merely omitted, since an omission does not shadow a still-present wildcard the way an explicit deny does. census_lock is not allowed at all: its own permission spec (`--wait * --emit --actor * -- bash -c '... asset_census.py *)`) has more than one trailing wildcard, which is not an expressible Claude Code Bash rule (rules are one fixed prefix plus a single trailing '*', never a multi-wildcard glob) -- census_run.py builds the one validated invocation itself instead. Bash(pg_dump ...), Bash(python3 platform/scripts/governance/*) and Bash(~/.config/suvarna/bin/suvarna-build --preflight*) are added so the documented analyst/builder commands are not refused on day one (B10); suvarna-build is allowed for --preflight only, never a bare invocation -- dispatch stays gated by the hold-guard hook. The PreToolUse hook now runs a wrapper script (hold_guard.sh) from the hq worktree via PYTHONPATH, so a broken import fails closed for Agent and dispatch-like Bash calls instead of exiting a non-2 code the harness reads as 'no objection' (S14).
